standards.name: Neuroscience Information Exchange Format (NIX)
standards.abstract: NIX is a generic data model and file format for storing fully annotated scientific datasets, developed for neuroscience (originally from the Electrophysiology Task Force of the INCF Datasharing Program). It targets experimental data such as time series, spike trains, images and ROIs, storing the primary data together with rich metadata and typed dimension descriptors (sampled, range, set, alias-range). The project is maintained by the German Neuroinformatics Node (G-Node) and published as an open-source library (C++ reference implementation) with language bindings and an HDF5 backend; its documentation describes entities, their relationships, and APIs for creating/reading/writing the model.

classification.rationale: The source material describes a structured data model with named entities and explicit relationships (an entity-relationship schema / inheritance and containment relations). It lists entities (File, Block, DataArray, Tag, MultiTag, Dimensions, Group, Section, Source, etc.) and shows how they contain or reference each other — this is best represented as a DAG of entities and relations rather than a flat table of fields or a prose checklist of principles.

File.name: File
File.description: On-disk container implementing the NIX model; current implementations store data using HDF5 as the storage backend.
File.evidence: The current implementations store the actual data using the HDF5 file format as a storage backend.

Block.name: Block
Block.description: A Block is a top-level container inside a File that hosts data entities (DataArrays, Tags, MultiTags, Groups, Sources, Sections, ...).
Block.evidence: open a file, create a block that will host the data

DataArray.name: DataArray
DataArray.description: The central entity for storing n-dimensional data together with label, unit and a dimension descriptor for each axis; requires a name and a type and stores data plus metadata.
DataArray.evidence: The DataArray is the most central entity of the NIX data model. As almost all other NIX-entities it requires a name and a type.

DataArray_storage_and_meta.name: DataArray (data + label/unit + dimensions)
DataArray_storage_and_meta.description: DataArray stores the actual data together with label and unit and requires dimension descriptors for each dimension.
DataArray_storage_and_meta.evidence: The DataArray stores the actual data together with label and unit. In addition, the DataArray needs a dimension descriptor for each dimension.

SampledDimension.name: SampledDimension
SampledDimension.description: Dimension descriptor for regularly sampled dimensions (sampling interval, offset, label, unit).
SampledDimension.evidence: SampledDimension: Used if a dimension is sampled at regular intervals.

RangeDimension.name: RangeDimension
RangeDimension.description: Dimension descriptor for irregularly sampled dimensions; stores explicit ticks (values) that must be numeric and ascending.
RangeDimension.evidence: RangeDimension: Used if a dimension is sampled at irregular intervals. ... The ticks of a RangeDimension must be numeric and ascending.

AliasRangeDimension.name: AliasRangeDimension
AliasRangeDimension.description: A special case of RangeDimension whose information is tied to the DataArray itself; used for event times and 1-D numeric arrays.
AliasRangeDimension.evidence: There is a special case of the RangeDimension, the AliasRangeDimension, which is used when e.g. event times are stored.

SetDimension.name: SetDimension
SetDimension.description: Dimension descriptor used for categorical dimensions where entries are labels rather than numeric positions.
SetDimension.evidence: SetDimension: Used for dimensions that represent categories rather than physical quantities.

Tag.name: Tag
Tag.description: Entity to tag points or regions in DataArrays; Tags reference DataArrays and provide positions/extents.
Tag.evidence: Data retrieval via Tag and MultiTag: Tags and MultiTags refer to DataArrays to tag points or regions in the data.

MultiTag.name: MultiTag
MultiTag.description: Like Tag, a MultiTag refers to DataArrays to tag multiple points/regions; used to annotate data segments across arrays.
MultiTag.evidence: Data retrieval via Tag and MultiTag: Tags and MultiTags refer to DataArrays to tag points or regions in the data.

Group.name: Group
Group.description: Named grouping entity (container) for organizing related entities inside a Block.
Group.evidence: nix::base::IBlock::createGroup (C++ function)  (listed in API index showing Block can create groups)

Section.name: Section
Section.description: Hierarchical metadata container; Sections can have child Sections and are used for structured metadata.
Section.evidence: For example a Block can have different Sections and Sources, while Sections and Sources can have different child Sections or Sources respectively and so on.

Source.name: Source
Source.description: Entity describing the origin of data (e.g., a recording device or experimental subject); Sources can be organized under Blocks and nested.
Source.evidence: For example a Block can have different Sections and Sources, while Sections and Sources can have different child Sections or Sources respectively and so on.

Feature.name: Feature
Feature.description: A Feature is an entity type attached to tags (IBaseTag provides createFeature) that links to data (a reference to a DataArray or subset).
Feature.evidence: nix::base::IBaseTag::createFeature (C++ function)  (listed in API index showing tags support features and references)

Property.name: Property
Property.description: A metadata property/value attached to entities (part of the metadata model).

DataFrame.name: DataFrame
DataFrame.description: A tabular (columnar) entity type for structured tabular data; listed as a model entity and API class in the documentation.
DataFrame.evidence: The addition of the Group entity or the DataFrame entity would be such a change.
